title: Breeding Program Planning Workbook
purpose: Provide a traceable working record for breeding objectives, parent qualification, controlled crosses, F1 evaluation, and F2 population planning.

sections.title: Target Product Profile
sections.decisionPrompt: Which traits are mandatory, which are desirable, and which tradeoffs are acceptable?

sections.title: Parent Qualification and Complementarity
sections.decisionPrompt: Does each parent contribute evidence-backed strengths that address the breeding objective without adding an unacceptable liability?

sections.title: Controlled Cross and Identity Record
sections.decisionPrompt: What evidence would require the seed lot to be downgraded from verified biparental parentage to uncertain parentage?

sections.title: F1 Family Evaluation

calculations.name: Mid-parent heterosis
calculations.formula: ((F1 mean - mid-parent mean) / mid-parent mean) x 100
calculations.limits: Use only when parent and F1 values were measured under comparable conditions and the trait scale supports percentage comparison.

sections.decisionPrompt: Does the measured family support a claim of useful F1 performance, and how much within-family variation remains?

sections.title: F2 Population and Selection Plan

calculations.name: Probability of at least one desired individual

variables.p: probability one individual has the desired combination

calculations.limits: This assumes the stated probability model is valid and does not correct for linkage, viability selection, classification error, or genotype-by-environment effects.

calculations.name: Population size for target confidence
calculations.limits: Round up and increase further for mortality, sex ratio, testing loss, linkage uncertainty, and the need to retain multiple families.

sections.decisionPrompt: Is the planned population large enough to recover the target combination with useful confidence while still allowing accurate measurement?

qualityRules: Do not substitute cultivar names for verified identity.
Do not convert an observed association into a heritable-trait claim without progeny evidence.
Do not describe an entire F1 or F2 family from one selected plant.
Preserve failed tests, deviations, and uncertain parentage in the record.
Keep exploratory breeding records separate from publication or release authorization.
